subject: Defining jurisdictional triggers & interim relief workflow for Solaris pilot
messages:
From: Chris Wong <chris.wong@solaristech.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@solaristech.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Solaris pilot — jurisdiction language and interim relief (first pass)

David —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. We're excited to move the pilot forward but Legal asked that we close the loop on a couple specific items in the MSA/order form before we execute:

1) Governing law & selected forum: they want either (a) California law with San Francisco courts as exclusive venue, or (b) Delaware law with arbitration for disputes.
2) Interim relief / injunctive relief: Solaris needs certainty that they can seek provisional remedies in a local court (to preserve IP and data) even if the remedy would otherwise be subject to arbitration.
3) Notice and escalation: they proposed a 10-business-day cure window and an escalation step to Redwood's Head of Legal before filing any emergency relief.

I've attached our marked MSA (first pass) — redlines mostly in Section 14 (Dispute Resolution) and Section 2 (Order Form carve). Can your legal team confirm whether Redwood can accept Solaris' carve for provisional measures, or propose alternate language that preserves Redwood's desire for arbitration?

Appreciate a quick read; our procurement needs to meet Solaris' internal GO/NO-GO by 7/6.

Best,
Chris
Head of Commercial Operations
Solaris Systems

Attachment: Solaris_MSA_redlines_20270629.pdf (PDF, 125KB)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Wong <chris.wong@solaristech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Solaris pilot — jurisdiction language and interim relief (first pass)

Chris —

Thanks for sending this over and for summarising the asks. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Karthik (sales) to finalize. Initial thoughts below so Solaris knows where we stand:

- Governing law: Redwood prefers Delaware law for commercial predictability, but California law is acceptable for a US-based consumer-facing pilot if coupled with a mutual waiver of jury trial.
- Forum/arbitration: Redwood's standard is to keep arbitration for contract-level disputes but allow courts to grant provisional relief. We can accept a carve that expressly preserves right to seek injunctive/provisional measures in a court of competent jurisdiction prior to/arising notwithstanding any arbitration clause — but need a narrow, reciprocal formulation.
- Interim relief workflow: we can agree to a short notice + escalation requirement (10 business days) for non-emergency matters. For emergency injunctive relief (e.g., theft of data or immediate IP risk), we cannot require a waiting period.

Marissa — can you propose redline language that: (i) preserves our arbitration posture, (ii) allows Solaris to seek provisional relief in court in narrow circumstances, and (iii) includes a short escalation path for commercial disputes? Also flag any exposure if we accept Solaris' proposed breadth on provisional remedies.

Karthik — timeline note: Solaris needs final by 7/6. If Legal needs more time, can we ask for a brief procurement extension?

Thanks —
David
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Chris Wong <chris.wong@solaristech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Solaris pilot — jurisdiction language and interim relief (first pass)

Chris / David —

Thanks for the clear summary. I've reviewed Solaris' marked MSA and drafted a concise compromise that we think balances Redwood's arbitration-first posture with Solaris' need for urgent remedies. Redline highlights below — full wording attached and pasted after the message.

Redline summary (high-level):
- Arbitration remains the exclusive forum for disputes arising under the Agreement, except that either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo or prevent irreparable harm. This carve is reciprocal and limited in scope (preservation only).
- Governing law: proposal to specify Delaware law for the Agreement; if Solaris insists on California, add a mutual jury-waiver and venue for provisional relief acknowledged as SF or County court.
- Emergency definition: "emergency" is limited to (a) imminent unauthorized data exfiltration, (b) misappropriation of trade secrets, or (c) actions that will cause irreparable competitive harm within 48 hours. For non-emergencies, require a 10-business-day notice and escalation to Redwood Legal (marissa.cole@redwood.ai) before filing.
- Remedies carve: Redwood retains right to seek any equitable relief but will use proportional scope (narrow, temporary injunctions rather than broad, indefinite restraints).

Attached: MSA_redline_MCole_20270629.pdf (same content as pasted below). Also attached an interim-relief flowchart to aid Procurement.

Proposed wording (paste-ready):
"Notwithstanding the Parties' agreement to submit disputes to binding arbitration, either Party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect such Party's confidential information, intellectual property, or to prevent the dissipation of assets, provided that such relief is narrowly tailored, reciprocal, and limited to preservation pending resolution of the dispute in arbitration. The right to seek provisional remedies shall not be construed to permit a Party to obtain substantive relief that would otherwise be available only through arbitration."

I view Solaris' original phrasing as broader than necessary. The above keeps our arbitration posture intact while giving Solaris the certainty they requested for true emergencies. If Solaris wants California law and SF venue, we can accommodate with the mutual jury waiver; otherwise propose Delaware law.

Chris — if Solaris Legal is comfortable with the phrasing above, we can finalize and route for signature. If they prefer a different definition of "emergency," please send a one-paragraph alternative and we'll respond quickly.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_redline_MCole_20270629.pdf; InterimRelief-Flowchart.png

This is great; appreciate the crisp compromise language. Solaris Legal reviewed your proposed clause and confirms they can accept the carve as written, with one small tweak to the emergency definition to explicitly include "unauthorized access to customer production data." They also prefer California law for this pilot (we're a CA-based legal entity) — we'd accept Delaware if Redwood is firm, but we'd like the mutual jury-waiver if you choose CA.

Next steps: we will incorporate Marissa's clause with the small addition and send a clean MSA + signed order form for countersignature tomorrow. Procurement can hold the internal GO until countersignature, so the 7/6 timeline still works.
